title: Natural Language Processing for the Legal Domain: A Survey of Tasks, Datasets, Models and Challenges

bias_targets.methodology: Reviewing evaluation benchmarks like FairLex that assess fairness in natural language processing models by tracking performance across sensitive attributes, including gender, region of origin, and defendant state.
Highlighting literature that evaluates predictive models by attempting to predict case outcomes based solely on judges' surnames to expose historical data bias.

Surveying bias and fairness as an Open Research Challenge, analyzing how historical legal decisions embedded in training data create feedback loops that amplify discrimination, and reviewing data anonymization techniques used to explore these biases.
